slides.title: SwachhRoute Delhi
slides.subtitle: Collect when needed. Route smart. Prove it's clean.
slides.description: An AI-assisted waste collection platform for Delhi, built on Dijkstra routing.
slides.speakerNote: Open with one sentence: 'Delhi's trucks drive fixed routes while bins overflow elsewhere. We fix that.'
bullets: Real-time IoT smart bin telematics across 14 Delhi localities
Dijkstra-powered shortest path and multi-truck fleet routing
Dynamic landfill load balancing for Ghazipur, Bhalswa & Okhla
Photo-verified citizen grievance resolution with cryptographic proof

slides.title: The Problem
slides.subtitle: Delhi's garbage chain breaks at five critical points.
slides.speakerNote: Pick one story the judges will recognise, such as an overflowing bin near a market, and tell it in two sentences.
bullets: Fixed-schedule pickups: Some bins overflow while other trucks run half-empty.
Three overloaded landfills (Ghazipur, Bhalswa, Okhla) and mostly mixed waste.
Illegal dumping spots keep returning, with zero data on root causes.
Complaints get lost, and nobody verifies they were actually resolved on-ground.
Trucks and workers are barely tracked, so municipal accountability is weak.

slides.title: Why Now?
slides.subtitle: The tools to solve Delhi's waste gridlock are finally cheap and open.
slides.speakerNote: The point is that this was not practical a few years ago, and now a small team can build it.
bullets: Low-power bin sensors (LoRa, ultrasonic) are affordable at city scale ($12-$20/unit).
Open road data (OpenStreetMap) and fast routing engines (Dijkstra, OSRM, OR-Tools) exist.
Vision AI can check a photo of a dump or a cleaned spot in milliseconds.
WhatsApp and voice reach workers who do not use complex English smartphone apps.
Landfill pressure makes every wasted trip and unsegregated tonne costly for MCD.

slides.title: The Solution
slides.subtitle: SwachhRoute decides when to collect, which route to take, and where to unload, then proves the job was done.
slides.speakerNote: Show the interactive prototype here if time allows.
bullets: Collect only bins that are full or about to overflow, not on a blind fixed schedule.
Build the shortest multi-stop route with Dijkstra and multi-truck time windows.
Send each truck to the landfill with capacity and shortest queue, not just the nearest one.
Let citizens report waste and receive AI photo proof with SHA-256 certificate upon cleanup.

slides.title: Nine Features, One Platform
slides.subtitle: Modular, end-to-end municipal waste intelligence suite.
slides.speakerNote: Do not read the table. Name the three groups (Smart Collection, Trust & Proof, People & Accountability) and give one example from each.

features.name: Fill Prediction
features.description: Forecasts which bins fill next using history, festivals (Diwali/Holi) and weather.

features.name: Multi-Truck Routing
features.description: Dijkstra distances plus vehicle routing planner with time windows.

features.name: Lane-Aware Routing
features.description: Traffic-aware edges and the right vehicle size (E-rickshaw vs tipper vs compactor) for narrow lanes.

features.name: Landfill Balancing
features.description: Picks unload site among Ghazipur, Bhalswa, Okhla by distance, queue and remaining capacity.

features.name: Photo-Verified Complaints
features.description: Citizen photo in, cleaned-spot photo out, AI checks both and issues SHA-256 certificate.

features.name: Dumping Heatmap
features.description: Shows repeat hotspots to place smart bins, CCTV or night sanitation patrols.

features.name: Segregation Intelligence
features.description: Labels wet, dry and hazardous waste with scrap valuation in ₹.

features.name: Worker Layer
features.description: Hindi app, WhatsApp alerts and IVR voice broadcasts, works offline.

features.name: Ward Dashboard
features.description: Ranks MCD wards on km saved, diesel, CO2 averted, overflow rate and SLA closure.

slides.title: How It Works
slides.subtitle: 6-stage autonomous workflow from sensor telemetry to municipal dashboard.
slides.speakerNote: Emphasise that Dijkstra is the core, and the other layers make it practical for a real city.
bullets: 1. Bin sensors and citizen reports stream real-time data to one unified API layer.
2. The forecast model predicts which bins will cross overflow threshold at pickup time.
3. Dijkstra builds a travel-time matrix on the Delhi road graph per vehicle type.
4. The planner assigns bins to trucks under capacity and shift time limits.
5. When a truck is full, the system dynamically picks the best landfill and inserts the unload stop.
6. Workers get the plan by app, WhatsApp or voice; officers see real-time progress on the dashboard.

slides.title: Product Demo & Technology
slides.subtitle: Interactive Delhi map with 14 locality bins, a central depot, and three landfills.
slides.speakerNote: Tell judges the prototype uses simulated fill levels and realistic distances, and that the production version integrates OpenStreetMap feeds and live LoRaWAN sensors.
bullets: Interactive Delhi map: 14 localities, central depot (IP Estate), 3 landfills (Ghazipur, Bhalswa, Okhla).
Live Dijkstra routing animation with step-by-step waypoint traversal.
Direct comparison: AI-optimized Dijkstra route saves 29.6% km and 35% fuel vs naive fixed route.
Tech Stack: FastAPI, Node/Express REST API, Leaflet GIS, React + Tailwind, Python Vision AI.

slides.title: What Makes It Different
slides.subtitle: Most smart-bin projects stop at 'bin is full, send a truck'. We go much further.
slides.speakerNote: Be candid that Dijkstra alone is not new. The novelty is combining prediction, planning, landfill balancing and verified proof in one Delhi-specific system.

slides.title: Market & Customers
slides.subtitle: Primary customer: Delhi's municipal bodies, starting with one willing MCD ward.
slides.speakerNote: Avoid quoting large market numbers you cannot source. A clear, bottom-up logic is more credible than a big figure.
bullets: Primary customer: Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) across 12 administrative zones.
Next customers: Other Indian Smart Cities, private waste contractors, RWAs, universities and industrial parks.
Sizing model: Bins in pilot ward × fee per bin/month + Trucks in fleet × fee per truck/month.

slides.title: Business Model
slides.subtitle: Sustainable software-as-a-service (SaaS) for municipal bodies and contractors.
slides.speakerNote: State that pricing will be set from pilot cost savings, since fuel savings per truck is the real value anchor.
bullets: Platform Subscription: Annual software fee per bin and per truck.
Pilot Setup & Sensor Integration: One-time deployment fee + hardware at cost.
Premium Modules: Urban planning analytics, carbon credit certification, API integrations.
Sponsored Programs: Corporate CSR and Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) partners.

slides.title: Competition & Positioning
slides.subtitle: SwachhRoute is positioned in the high-intelligence, high-verification quadrant.
slides.speakerNote: Name real competitors you have researched when you present, and say specifically what they do not cover.
bullets: Citizen Complaint Apps (Swachhata App): Lacks routing intelligence and predictive dispatch.
Basic Smart-Bin Hardware Sellers: Sell sensors without route optimization or landfill balancing.
Fleet Tracking Software (GPS only): Tracks trucks without fill prediction or photo-proof verification.
SwachhRoute Delhi: Combines predictive routing with verified visual proof in one system.

slides.title: Go-To-Market Strategy
slides.subtitle: 5-phase rollout from single-ward pilot to NCT-wide scale.
slides.speakerNote: Be clear that government sales are slow, which is why private campuses and societies are the early revenue path.
bullets: 1. Pilot Ward: Agree on clear baseline success metrics with one MCD Ward Officer (e.g. Ward 112 CP).
2. Fast-Moving Customers: Deploy on large university campuses, tech parks, and gated societies.
3. Government Route: Leverage India Smart Cities Challenge and MCD Innovation MoU.
4. Field Partners: Onboard local waste-picker collectives and informal sector aggregators.
5. Proof as Marketing: The public ward scorecard shows hard results and creates demand from neighbouring wards.

slides.title: Impact & Success Metrics
slides.subtitle: Proving measurable ROI within 90 days in the pilot ward.
slides.speakerNote: Say clearly that these are goals to be measured against baseline.

slides.title: Project Roadmap
slides.subtitle: 4 development phases with strict validation gates.
slides.speakerNote: Stress that each phase starts only after its gate is met.

phases.gate: 80% of complaints closed with verified AI proof.

slides.title: The Ask
slides.subtitle: We are asking for a pilot ward, not a city-wide contract.
slides.speakerNote: Make the ask specific and small enough that saying yes is easy.
bullets: One pilot MCD ward (e.g. Ward 112 / Connaught Place) and its sanitation staff for a 90-day pilot.
Access to current truck routes, bin locations, and grievance logs for that ward.
A designated contact officer at MCD for weekly operational review.
Incubation grant / mentor support for LoRaWAN sensor hardware prototyping.

slides.title: Closing Vision
slides.subtitle: Delhi doesn't need more trucks. It needs smarter trips and proof that the work is done.
slides.speakerNote: End on the one-line vision, then stop and take questions.
bullets: Smarter routes. Cleaner streets. A healthier Delhi.

judgeQA.question: Is Dijkstra new?
judgeQA.answer: No. We use Dijkstra as the proven, fast routing core and build prediction, multi-truck planning, lane-width constraints, landfill balancing, and verified proof around it.

judgeQA.question: Why not use Google Maps routing?
judgeQA.answer: Our needs go beyond a single point-to-point route: we solve multi-bin, multi-truck combinatorial vehicle routing with weight capacities, narrow lane vehicle restrictions, and landfill queue balancing.

judgeQA.question: What if sensors fail or are stolen?
judgeQA.answer: The system falls back to historical time-series regression estimates and flags missing sensor telemetry for inspection. The pilot begins with tamper-resistant ultrasonic pods.

judgeQA.question: How will sanitation workers use it?
judgeQA.answer: We provide a simplified bilingual Hindi/English PWA with offline caching, turn-by-turn guidance, automated WhatsApp alert dispatch, and IVR voice call integration.

judgeQA.question: What about citizen privacy with grievance photos?
judgeQA.answer: Faces and vehicle license plates are automatically blurred before storage. Data retention is strictly bounded and aggregated in compliance with Indian DPDP Act.
